intro.title: Rate limiting & security headers
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure Express.js server that protects against excessive requests and common web vulnerabilities. You will learn to implement rate limiting to control how many requests a client can make in a given time period, preventing abuse. Additionally, you will set security headers to defend against attacks like cross-site scripting (XSS) and clickjacking. The main technologies used are the Express framework, the `express-rate-limit` middleware for rate limiting, and the `helmet` middleware for security headers. By the end, you'll have a server that is more resilient and safer for real-world use.
intro.usecase: Rate limiting and security headers are essential for protecting production APIs from abuse and attacks. You'll implement these in Express when building public-facing endpoints like user registration forms, payment processing APIs, or dashboard data feeds. For example, an e-commerce site uses rate limiting to prevent bots from brute-forcing login attempts, while security headers like Content-Security-Policy protect customer dashboards from XSS attacks. As a developer, you'll configure these safeguards to ensure your applications remain available and secure under real traffic conditions.
